title: The St. Louis Merrymakers; Herschel Evans joins Troy Floyd
summary: Tate switches to tenor in the St. Louis Merrymakers, and Herschel Evans leaves for Troy Floyd's band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So Milton went back to Dallas. So during the time -- I had been like playing tenor anyway, switching, you know, like that month he stayed up there. So I was playing his tenor. I didn't own a tenor, but I was playing his tenor, just in case. I says, "Well, when you leave -- I know you're going to leave, so when you leave, I'm just going to switch to this tenor and get me a tenor," I said, because I liked the way he played tenor. Herschel liked the way he played tenor, too. We used to listen to him, you know. He could play, Gary.
Are you and Herschel about the same age?

No, he's -- Herschel's about three and a half years older, maybe four. Herschel and Lester and Ben and Budd-- Budd's a little older than I am, but Budd, I don't think Budd is quite as old as Herschel and Lester. They're all around the same age. They would be now about -- oh, it would be about 70 now. So, you know.

But anyway, we stayed out there with that band and I played tenor in that band. That was the St. Louis Merry-makers, that was the name of that band. Now that was like the first band that I worked with after leaving the McCloud's Night Owls. They called the band the St. Louis Merrymakers.

So then Troy Floyd was pretty -- name band then, you know. It was a bigger name than the St. Louis Merrymakers. So a friend of Herschel's had been trying to get him in that band for a long, long time and the tenor player that was playing in the band was a tenor player by the name of Funny Bagsby and he quit the band, Funny Bagsby was his name. I never forget. So Herschel joined that band. They told him they'd let him play tenor and that's when he went to Troy Floyd to play tenor. And I later played with him, you know, also, and we used to alternate. He'd play tenor some and I'd play alto, because we were both alto players.
